_comment: Golden vectors for the ladder's target/stop math.
This math exists TWICE: core/exits.py computes what is actually traded, and
LadderModal's preview shows the user what they are about to arm. Two
implementations of one formula, in two languages, with nothing holding them
together — and they drifted: the dialog measured the first-buy offset from
the highest level it displayed while the backend measured it from the
highest level posted, so a 200-point target was stored as 600 and inherited
Both sides now assert against this file. If either changes, its test fails.

target.name: first rung anchors on its own entry, full offset
chained rung anchors on the rung above it
chain percent shrinks the offset, not the anchor
percent mode computes the offset on the anchor
percent mode chained: offset comes off the ANCHOR price, not the entry
anchor below entry would exit instantly -> falls back to self-anchored
zero chain percent still cannot target at or below entry

sl.name: points stop sits its offset below the entry
percent stop computes on the entry
stop-losses disabled means exactly zero, the engine's 'no stop'
offset wider than the price computes at or below zero (refused at entry)
